$comment: The composition of the process per tier. JSON configures, Python validates.
The separation of powers is strict and deliberate. THE COMPOSITION stands HERE: which
steps on which tier, how many rungs the ladder has, how many convergence rounds, which
gates are human. LEGALITY stands in stages.py: the stage names, the allowed transitions
and this file's schema. A typo in a stage name is refused with a message before the
first write, never carried out.
The reason this file exists: a change with 4 requirements and 143 lines of code went
through the strategic tier, because a conversation set the tier before anything was
known -- and the mechanism for shortening the chain existed, had tests and was not used.
Three asymmetries pushed upwards: a default p2 in the middle of the scale, one-sided
friction (raising is always allowed, lowering is not) and no arithmetic anchor.
This file removes the third, and `detection` below is that anchor.
schema_version 2: a value in `conditional` may be a list of signals with `any_of`
semantics. Version 1 knew only one signal per step, so a reader of that version would
look at a list and not know they were looking at something else.
schema_version 3: `convergence_last_round` replaced by `convergence_deep_rounds`
(a number) -- how many of the FIRST convergence rounds are a full hunt; every round
above that only verifies the recorded resolutions. No key = every round deep (the
behaviour before #30). A version 2 reader would ignore the new key and run every round
as a hunt by authors -- which is exactly the quiet divergence that versioning is meant
to protect against.
schema_version 4: `boundary` -- what a stage boundary does after the stage commit. A
version 3 reader ignores an unknown top-level key, so it would close a stage, skip the
retro and say nothing; and a retro nobody runs is the defect this key was added to fix.
That is exactly the silence the version number exists to break.
schema_version 5: the glossary under `detection.signals` describes the engine's six
specification signals and nothing else. The path signals (backend_touched, frontend_touched,
infra_touched, tooling_touched, ci_touched) are this stack's -- declared, described and
measured from .specconf/stack.json -- and this file may condition steps on them without
describing them a second time. A version-4 reader would accept a glossary that no longer
describes the path signals and measure them from a file it does not read; the number is
what tells it to stop.
schema_version 6: `tiers.*.max_lines` is WITHDRAWN -- the per-artefact line budgets are
gone from this file and no reader replaces them. The audit measured all six budgets on
one change and found all six exceeded, delta.md at 24x, with every stage closing anyway:
the engine printed a multiplier and refused nothing, so a number here was advice wearing
the shape of a rule. The numbers this file carried were also byte-identical to the
Flutter template's, which says they were copied rather than measured on this stack --
so they are withdrawn, not re-derived. delta.md is now the BRIEF -- one entry per path,
everything an earlier pass said assembled beside it into delta-history.md -- so it is
bounded by what it IS, and an artefact nobody can shorten is a finding about the skill
that writes it rather than a line to trim. A version-5 reader tolerates the key, reads
it with nothing and NAMES it as withdrawn; that reader would also look at this profile,
see no budget anywhere and conclude the artefacts are measured somewhere it has not
looked. The number is what tells it they are not.
Tier = the maximum of what the signals imply. A new context is always p3.
`cr-impact` computes the signals, grepping surface names against the specification
tree, and RECORDS them with the verb `change_state.py set-signals` --
that same record then selects the conditional steps below. There is no second decision
and no second place in which somebody could take it differently.
The order matters: the first match wins, heaviest first.
`rule_touched` exists because `default: p0` merged two different facts: "I measured
no signal" and "there is no behaviour change". A business-rule change inside a
single context -- the commonest class of change in this system -- is not named in
api.md, data-model.md or ui/, so it fell to p0: no requirements, no integration tests,
and traceability and requirements passed as NOT_APPLICABLE, because traceability counts only the changes
that have a requirements.md.
A quiet skip of art. III looked exactly like a change that requires nothing.
The six signals described under `signals` below are the engine's, measured against
the specification tree on every stack. The path signals the rules and `conditional`
also name -- backend_touched, frontend_touched, infra_touched, tooling_touched,
ci_touched -- are this stack's: .specconf/stack.json declares them, says why each
exists and which paths light it. This file conditions on them and describes none of
them twice.

signals.contract_touched: the surface's name occurs in spec/design/api.md or in contracts/openapi/*.yaml
signals.rule_touched: the name occurs as a BR-* rule or a P-* flow in spec/contexts/*.md
signals.contexts_touched_gt_1: the change touches more than one spec/contexts/*.md
signals.new_context: a domain concept absent from glossary.md and from every context

$comment: A step listed here runs ONLY when any of its signals is lit. A step absent from here
always runs when the tier lists it in `steps`. The value is a signal or a list of
signals -- one operator, `any_of`, the same one as in `detection.rules` above.
This is the second half of note 14 and without it the first half is harmful: a fine
split of the skills lowers the cost only when it is paired with selection. A narrow
skill costs less per run (12 turns), a broad one more (61 turns), and a skill that
does not run costs nothing.
THE RULE FOR CHOOSING A CONDITION: a step's condition is the same predicate as the
gate that would fail without that step. recorded-decision asks whether `spec/design/**`,
`spec/contexts/**` or `spec/invariants.md` moved -- so `design-adr` is not listed
here and runs on every tier with a design phase, because every tier >= p1 has some
specification signal lit by definition. screen-spec asks about a screen, so `design-ui` is
conditioned on `screen_touched`. Where a condition and a gate diverge, exceptions are
born -- and that is the measurable definition of a well-chosen condition rather than
a matter of taste.
`build-tests-unit` is deliberately NOT listed here. Every behaviour change carries
at least one test that was seen red -- that is the constitution, art. III, and
conditioning it on a signal would be an emergency exit with no expiry date.
A NOTE ON EVIDENCE. The measurements cited in this file come from runs of the
PREVIOUS product and their change records were not moved into this repository:
`spec/changes/` held no record when this was written (CR-2609-9b1e, reconciled by hand, is the first), so the CR-2608-* identifiers below do not resolve here and
cannot be opened. These are measured numbers rather than invented ones, and that is
why they stay -- but they are a quotation from outside, not a reference. The first
change record carried out in this tree replaces them with evidence that can be
opened; until then none of them is falsifiable by a reader. (The 2026-09-01 audit
found four of them, one pointing at a non-existent `retro/notes/` file.)
`build-tests-e2e` stood on `contract_touched` alone and that was too narrow a half
of the sentence. Measured on CR-2608-f9b6: a new bounded context, a new table,
a new screen -- and ZERO files under `e2e/`. A screen and a schema change the
system's observable behaviour at least as much as a new endpoint does, so the
condition is now the union of three signals, and with all three absent the change
really is a micro-correction with no trace on the API, UI or data side. The gate that
watches this is e2e-scenario.
`infra_touched`, `tooling_touched` and `ci_touched` condition exactly three steps and
not one more. `design-architecture`, because the question "where is this to live"
is the same question for a Terraform module as for a service. `design-testing`,
because those three trees DO have an evidence surface and nobody chooses it
deliberately: 11 fitness functions read infra/ as text, tests/tooling/ reads
scripts/, and CI parity with check.sh is a test. And `build-platform`, from
2026-09-17 (#30): the third was the one missing, and its absence is what made the
other two dishonest. Two design steps asked where a Terraform module should live and
how it would be proved, and then the implement wave held nobody who could write it --
so the answer arrived as a refusal after the work, rather than as a member of the
fan-out. A signal that changes the tier and summons a designer owes the wave an author.
`build-platform` is in the `implement` list of EVERY tier, p0 included, although no
p0 change can light its signals -- `detection.rules` puts all three at p1. p0 is there
for the repair tail, which computes its composition from a fix's scope rather than
from the tier: the engine asks `members(P0, IMPLEMENT, {signal})` of every signal an
implementer is conditioned on, and a member missing from that list is a fix nobody can
carry out. `build-tests-unit` gained the same three signals in `fix_conditional` for
the other half of it: a builder dispatched with no test author is a repair with no RED
proof, and tests/fitness/ -- that member's tree -- is exactly where the detectors that
read infra/, .github/ and scripts/ as text live.
`build-backend` answers `tooling_touched` as well as `backend_touched`, which is the
second half of the same repair. `scripts/` is in ITS write set and the engine holds it
there by name (test_sdd_skill_gate.py `_SHARED_PLUMBING`, bought by CR-2608-6fb2), so
the author for a scripts-only change could not be moved -- it had to be summoned. Of
the two fixes #30 offered, this is the one the engine leaves open. `build-platform`
owns the REST of `tooling_touched`: .claude/skills/ and docker-compose.yml.
What they deliberately do NOT condition: `design-api`, `design-data`, `design-ui`
and `design-spec` -- an infrastructure change has no contract, column or screen
and no business rule to describe, and a step with no subject produces an artefact
the next convergence round has to reconcile against nothing.
This applies ONLY when the composition is computed by a fix's scope (fix_scope
written by triage, read by fix_scope_of). On a review_fix tail the UNION of both
tables applies, and an entry from here wins; a step absent from the union always
runs -- reconcile-docs has no entry, so the shape of p0's spec_sync comes out of the
arithmetic when the fix touches no spec surface.
Why a second table rather than entries in `conditional`: build-tests-unit is
deliberately unconditional (the constitution, art. III -- every change has pure
rules to prove), and reconcile-spec/reconcile-design were deliberately not
conditioned on the signals of the WHOLE change -- a finer split needs a recorded
boundary, and a fix's tail is exactly that second point of measurement.
The measurement: CR-2608-8e96, attempt 11 -- the review_fix -> implement return
sent the full composition and three of wave 1's five dispatches (unit, integration,
e2e) had nothing to write; the gate refuses a zero write-set, cost: three full opus
contexts and a human decision. The retro note from that round is not in this tree --
see A NOTE ON EVIDENCE above.
THE REQUIREMENTS FAMILY JOINED THIS TABLE ON 2026-09-23 (#60), and until it did the
narrowing did not exist for it: a member absent from the union always runs, so a
review_fix return to `requirements` dispatched cr-impact, cr-requirements and
cr-scenarios unconditionally. On the other stack that round cost $40.94 -- as much as
the change it repaired (claude-marketplace#196). The engine reads a fix's scope for
`requirements` and `design` as it always did for `implement` and `spec_sync`
(forge 0.1.100); the values are this template's, and these three entries are them.
THE CUT IS BETWEEN READING AN EARLIER STAGE'S OUTPUT AND RE-AUTHORING IT. `impact.md`
records how the area worked BEFORE the change, and a repair does not move the past, so
the tail reads it and `cr-impact` stays home. Its two signals say the repair's area is
larger than the one the record described: `new_context` is a concept no context and no
glossary covers, `contexts_touched_gt_1` a second context the first pass had no reason
to read.
The other two are derived from their consumers rather than chosen, and the rule is the
mirror of the builder's: A CONSUMER NEVER GOES OUT WITHOUT THE AUTHOR OF WHAT IT
REQUIRES. `cr-scenarios` carries the union of the conditions of the three members that
require `scenarios.md`: build-tests-e2e (contract, screen, schema), build-tests-uat
(screen, contract, rule) and build-tests-integration (backend, schema, from this table).
The last is this stack's own and is why `backend_touched` is here and not on flutter:
the integration author refuses to invent a fixture value and takes every one from
`scenarios.md § Test data`, so a backend repair that dispatches it needs that section's
author too. A backend-only repair therefore sends two authors, not one -- that is not a
missed narrowing, it is the narrowing #60 § 13 forbids, turned down.
`cr-requirements` carries every signal this stack declares, and that is arithmetic
rather than a shrug: design-spec requires `requirements.md` and is unconditional, so
every scope that reaches the design stage needs the requirement, and build-tests-unit
and build-tests-uat require it too. It is written out rather than left absent because
absence and completeness read the same to the engine and differently to a person:
absence is the state this table was in before, and it says nobody measured.
tests/fitness/test_repair_composition.py holds all of it and turns red the day a
signal or a worker is added without this table being decided again.

p0.label: correction
$comment: No design phase, but WITH documentation: p0 lights no specification signal, so
there is no delta to reconcile here -- there is, however, a line for a human, and
that runs on every tier (the user's decision,
That is why `spec_sync` on p0 is `reconcile-docs` alone. `reconcile-spec` and
`reconcile-design` work DIFFERENTIALLY against what the `design/delta/*.md`
fragments promised -- and p0 has no design phase, so those fragments do not exist
and the difference is taken against nothing. `reconcile-design` is at the same time
the most expensive skill in the catalogue (61 turns, 9.54 M of context against
`design-api`'s 12 turns), so the cheapest tier was paying the most expensive author
for work it had nothing to perform on.
We do not condition them on a signal, although `conditional` could carry it:
"any specification signal lit" is exactly the same sentence as "tier >= p1",
and two sentences about one fact are checked in only one place. A finer split --
`reconcile-spec` for `spec/contexts/**`, `reconcile-design` for `spec/design/**` --
needs a RECORDED boundary of the change, and that comes into being at the design
phase's boundary. That is a second point of measurement and separate work.
`build-tests-integration` is here conditionally, and that is a patch over a hole
in the evidence: p0 with `app/` touched got `build-backend` with not a single test
touching the database.

p1.label: minor
$comment: The same chain of stages as p2 and a NARROWER composition -- because that is what
a saving that does not delete the evidence looks like. The design fan-out is full
as to NAMES and narrow as to the RUN: steps enter by signal, so a p1 touching the
contract alone sends two authors rather than seven.
Four steps came here from p2, each for a reason that was a defect:
`design-adr`, because `design-api` edits `spec/design/api.md`, so recorded-decision's condition
is lit, and the step that writes an ADR was absent -- p1 ALWAYS had to reach for
the escape sentence `**ADR:** none`. `design-testing`, because p1 wrote into four
test suites with no test strategy. `design-architecture`, because p1 sends
`build-backend` and `build-frontend` in one wave, and it is precisely this step
that lays out the disjoint write sets. `build-tests-uat`, because the script for a
human did not run on the tier `screen_touched` triggers -- that is, exactly where
a change is visible to a human.
`design-data` joined the list together with `build-migration`, which was already
here: a tier that builds a migration with no step that designs it is a migration
nobody designed. Both have the same condition, so on an ordinary p1 (where
`schema_touched` is dark by the definition of the detection rules) neither runs.

p3.label: strategic
$comment: The only tier with `design-domain` -- a new bounded context is the one signal
that is not up for negotiation. The rest of the composition is identical to p2, and
the difference sits in the number of convergence rounds: eight authors write into
one reality and have twenty-eight pairs in which they can diverge.
`convergence_deep_rounds: 1` on p2 and p3 exists out of measurement and is an
answer to a ladder that was a fixpoint on a moving target. A round re-dispatched
the AUTHORS with the instruction "re-derive your artefact", so each produced new
content, and `review-coherence` had one mode -- a full hunt -- so by construction
it could find in that content something that had not been there before. Measured on
CR-2608-f9b6: the `design` stage was 4 coherence passes, 4 reconciliations and 4
waves of authors, 26 dispatches, 154 USD and four hours; `requirements` 157 USD
over 21 dispatches; the artefacts exceeded their line budgets by 2.75x and 3.68x.
One deep round paid for itself and that can be shown with a number rather than an
impression: `COH-requirements-7` caught a contradiction between the answer to Q-8
and `spec/design/api.md` that two authors and the whole reconciliation had walked
past. The price of the verifying rounds is named too: they stop being a chance at a
finding nobody has named yet -- and one such existed (`COH-requirements-12`, caught
only on the third pass). Whoever wants a second hunt on p3 raises this number to 2
-- that is data, not code.
The authors do not re-derive in a round: they get the recorded resolutions to
apply with a minimal diff, and the judge gets the memory of the findings with their
resolutions and computes the round's mode itself in preflight. p0 has no rounds,
and p1 has no key: its only round is the first, so it is deep by arithmetic.
The budgets that do not depend on the tier. Exceeding one is a WARNING naming what
to cut -- not a refusal. A gate that blocks work over one line too many is a gate
people route around.
`coherence_files: 1` is hard and is here out of measurement: one change produced 24
COH-* files and 1 677 lines for 4 requirements, and then 24 separate calls to close
them. There is to be one report, with a section per pass.
What a stage boundary does once the stage's commit has landed. A boundary is a
session's end -- the message tells the user to open a new window -- so it is the last
moment at which the session that lived the work can say anything true about it.
`retro`: which boundaries run `/sdd-retro`. `every_stage` archives every session,
which is what gate `session-archives` already expects: one archive per session.
`gated_stages` narrows it to the tier's own `human_gates` when the transcripts prove
too heavy for the repository. `never` restores the behaviour that produced zero
archives in this repository over the whole of its history.
`push`: `auto` pushes the branch at the boundary on the strength of THIS setting;
`ask` puts the question to the user, which is what happened before. Neither can reach
`deliver`'s own push -- that one fires before the stage closes and keeps its human
gate, because it is the push a pull request is opened on top of.
